name: Greece
tagline: Six thousand islands, of which two hundred and twenty-seven are inhabited, and a mainland almost nobody visits.
summary: Greece is more mountain than island by area, and the mainland — Epirus, the Pindus, the Peloponnese — is emptier and greener than the postcards suggest. The islands divide into groups with different architecture, food and weather; the Cyclades are white and windy, the Ionians green, the Dodecanese medieval. Everything closes down in the afternoon heat and reopens at six, which is not laziness but sense.

season.note: May, June, September and early October are the sweet spot: swimmable sea, open tavernas, tolerable ruins. August is the whole of Greece and half of Europe on the same ferries. Many island businesses close entirely from November to April.

getting_around: Ferries are the network: fast catamarans and slow open-deck boats, both booked online and both cancelled by wind. Domestic flights save a day to the far islands. The mainland needs a car; the Athens metro is excellent and has an archaeological museum inside a station.
food: Whatever is in the pot that day — ask to see the kitchen, which is normal
Greek salad with no lettuce, and bread to finish the oil
Wine from Santorini's assyrtiko and Naoussa's xinomavro, both serious and both cheap here

festivals.name: Orthodox Easter — the biggest event of the year
Athens & Epidaurus Festival, in ancient theatres

know: Ferry cancellations for wind are common and not negotiable; leave a buffer day before a flight home.
Many older buildings ask you to bin paper rather than flush it — follow the sign.
Archaeological sites close early in winter and midday shade is scarce; go at opening.

regions.name: Athens & the Peloponnese
regions.summary: The classical core: the Acropolis, Mycenae, Olympia and a peninsula of castles and empty coast.

cities.name: Athens
cities.summary: A sprawling modern capital with a 2,500-year-old temple on a rock in the middle and a food scene that got very good, quietly.
highlights: The Acropolis at opening, and the Acropolis Museum afterwards, in that order
The National Archaeological Museum, which is the real prize
Rooftop bars looking at a floodlit Parthenon
Anafiotika, a Cycladic village accidentally inside the city

experiences.name: The Acropolis Museum, third floor
experiences.summary: The Parthenon frieze laid out at actual scale and orientation, with plaster casts where the British Museum holds the originals — the gaps are the argument.

cities.name: Nafplio
cities.summary: Greece's first capital: Venetian, neoclassical, under two fortresses, on a gulf in the Peloponnese.
highlights: Palamidi fortress and its 999 steps
Epidaurus's theatre, where a coin dropped on stage is audible in the back row
Mycenae's lion gate, forty minutes north

experiences.name: The acoustics at Epidaurus
experiences.summary: Sit in the top row and have someone whisper on the orchestra floor. Built in the 4th century BC and still unexplained in full.

cities.name: Monemvasia
cities.summary: A Byzantine town hidden on the seaward side of a rock island, invisible from the mainland.
highlights: A single gate, and no cars inside the walls
The upper town's ruins and Hagia Sophia on the summit
Swimming off the rocks below the walls

regions.name: The Islands
regions.summary: Cyclades, Dodecanese, Ionian and Crete — related, and not remotely the same.

cities.name: Naxos
cities.summary: The largest Cycladic island: mountain villages, marble quarries, a working agricultural interior and long sandy beaches.
highlights: The Portara, a temple doorway on an islet at the harbour
Halki and the mountain villages, with citron distilleries
An unfinished 6th-century BC kouros lying in a field where it cracked

experiences.name: The interior, not the beach
experiences.summary: Half the island is farmland at altitude — cheese, potatoes and Venetian towers, twenty minutes from the sand.

cities.name: Santorini
cities.summary: The rim of a drowned volcano, with villages on the edge of a 300-metre cliff and vines grown in baskets on the ground.
highlights: Akrotiri: a Bronze Age town buried in ash and preserved whole
Assyrtiko from vines trained into wreaths against the wind
The caldera path from Fira to Oia — walked early, not at sunset

experiences.name: Vines grown in baskets
experiences.summary: No trellises: the vines are woven into circles on the ground to shelter the fruit from wind and catch night moisture.

cities.name: Chania, Crete
cities.summary: A Venetian harbour with an Ottoman quarter behind it, on an island large enough to be its own country.
highlights: The Venetian lighthouse and the harbour arc
Samaria gorge: 16 km down through the White Mountains to the sea
Cretan food — the diet the research is about — in mountain villages

experiences.name: Down the Samaria gorge
experiences.summary: Sixteen kilometres, one direction only, ending at a boat because there is no road out. Open May to October.

cities.name: Rhodes
cities.summary: A walled medieval city built by crusader knights, on an island of Ottoman villages and butterfly valleys.
highlights: The largest inhabited medieval town in Europe, inside four kilometres of wall
Lindos's acropolis above a white village and a bay
Ottoman baths and mosques the guidebooks skip

regions.name: Northern Greece
regions.summary: Meteora's monasteries on rock pillars, Epirus's stone villages, and Thessaloniki's food.

cities.name: Meteora (Kalambaka)
cities.summary: Six working monasteries on top of sandstone pillars, reached for centuries by rope ladder and net.
highlights: The footpaths between monasteries, which almost every visitor drives instead
Frescoes inside Varlaam and Great Meteoron
Sunset from the rocks, not from the coach park

experiences.name: The old monks' paths
experiences.summary: Stone-cut trails link the pillars through the woods; three hours on foot beats a whole day by road.

cities.name: Thessaloniki
cities.summary: Greece's second city: Byzantine, Ottoman and Sephardic layers, and the country's most confident food.
highlights: The Rotunda and the Byzantine churches on the UNESCO list
Modiano and Kapani markets, then bougatsa for breakfast
The waterfront walk to the Umbrellas at dusk

cities.name: Zagori (Monodendri)
cities.summary: Forty-six stone villages in the Pindus mountains, linked by packhorse bridges over the deepest gorge in the world by ratio.
highlights: The Vikos gorge, from the Oxya viewpoint or from inside it
Arched stone bridges built by 18th-century merchant guilds
Bears, wolves and 1,800 plant species in the national park
